Commentary.Commentary: So that is it from this game! It is Pakistan who will enter the second Test with the lead. A must-win game for South Africa if they want to avoid a series defeat. It begins on the 4th of February at 1000 local (0500 GMT). Till then, take care and goodbye!

Pakistan skipper, Babar Azam, starts by saying the players played really well, the bowlers began brilliantly. States they wanted to bat first after winning the toss but they were asked to field first. Mentions partnerships were very important here and they were in a spot of bother but Azhar Ali and Fawad Alam did brilliantly, they were patient and batted excellently and them along with the bowlers gave them this victory. Adds South Africa is a quality side but they had plans for them and Nauman Ali was excellent on his debut along with Yasir Shah.

South African skipper, Quinton de Kock, says how they batted in the first innings cost them. Admits they failed to adjust to the wicket and a lot of dismissals were very soft. Mentions they will learn from this, their bowlers bowled really well but the Pakistan batters batted really well.

MAN OF THE MATCH, Fawad Alam, says this knock was very important as his side needed runs. Mentions they wanted to bat long in the first innings as that would make it easier for them in the second. Admits he was under pressure, especially as he is making a comeback after a long time. He though is enjoying his time and he thanks almighty for everything. States the pitch was not easy to bat on but he wanted to apply himself and not think a lot about the wicket.
Stay tuned for the presentation...

After gaining such a lead, one just got a feeling that South Africa would just surrender but they showed great fight and determination. They wiped out the deficit with 9 wickets in hand. Rassie and Markram showed great grit and determination to fight it out there. However, the last hour of the third day just changed the look of the game completely. Yasir got the ball to do its bit and he along with Nauman Ali ran through the middle and the top order of South Africa. There was not a lot of fight shown by the lower-order in the morning of Day 4 which saw Pakistan needing just 88 to win the first Test and they have done it without breaking a sweat.

Then, they were in trouble at 33 for 4 at the end of Day 1 but top class contributions from the lower and the middle order saw them gain a lead of over 150. Fawad Alam was the star with the bat for them as he smashed yet another ton after his comeback into the side.

South Africa did show fight throughout the game! They did have their moments but it was Pakistan who won the crucial moments and hence, they are the ones who have come out on top. First they managed to keep South Africa to 220 after being asked to field despite the visitors being 100 for 2 at one stage.

A very comfortable win in the end for Pakistan! Babar Azam's tenure as captain has started off with a win! It was never in doubt to be honest when they needed just under 90. South Africa did manage to take two quick wickets but that was all. Azhar Ali and Babar Azam with a 50-run plus stand, has ensured the home side take a 1-0 lead in this series.

We are back for the second session of Day 4. The South African players are out in the middle. Imran Butt and Abid Ali will resume their innings for Pakistan. Anrich Nortje will start the proceedings for this session.
... Day 4, Session 2 ...

Okay. A quarter of the target wiped off. Pakistan looked to be in a bit of discomfort but that was more because of the short span of time to bat before the break. The odd ball kept low, shot out but nothing really to alarm the batsmen. They will look to come out after the break and get a 10-wicket win. The Proteas did not have much time to force any issue, but will come out with some desperation after Lunch. Losing is not enjoyable but a 10-wicket defeat will sting more. This is a big break and the action will start only at 1.30 pm local (0830 GMT). It is a 90-minute session but should be enough to be the final one of the match. Get refreshed but do come back for the final rites.

FOUR! Nicely driven. A fullish ball on middle, Butt leans on it and drives this one straight down the ground past the mid on fielder for a boundary. What a nice way for Pakistan to end this session. With that, it will be, LUNCH ON DAY 4.

Interesting call! The Tendulkar-McGrath-Bucknor moment revisited. The shoulder before the wicket case opens up again. A short ball, around middle, Butt looks to duck, looking at the length. But the ball shoots extremely low. Hits him on the back and Rabada appeals. There is no conviction in the appeal but de Kock goes for the review. He then smiles, probably indicating that it is taken just for the sake of it. Impact outside leg and ball going down leg too. Wonder if Sachin Tendulkar is watching this game and wishing, had DRS been around in that Australia-India game! Review lost, if it matters.
